_comment: d1 #247 FoTI extension -- Wilovan's INN register, gated on brothers_job_done (the close of a_gentlemans_disagreement). Attached ONLY to the wilovan_inn_guest entity; the parlor hub (invrisil_wilovan) never rides along, so the commission, the three doors, Coyle, Farley, the marker and the fence shelf ALL stay in Invrisil -- and no follow-up to that quest may appear here in any form. REGISTER-PURE for a Gentleman Caller also means the trade is never NAMED: everything oblique, a colleague and an errand and a gentleman who keeps late hours, and not one word about what the Brothers do for a living. Ratici is present only as 'my colleague' (he is a shipped character, but this register does not do names, and his own lane is elsewhere). The hat is the tell, and tonight it means nothing. Serve mirrors selys_inn/zevara_inn: {once_per_waking, item} sanctioned compound, four one-verb effect dicts. Voice per docs/design/character-profiles.md: 'sir' address, apology-before-courtesy, one dash per line and this file spends none.

greet.speaker: Wilovan
greet.text: Sir. A good evening to you, and a very good room to have it in. No business tonight, you'll be relieved to hear. A gentleman does occasionally sit somewhere nobody owes anybody anything.

options.text: Bring him a bowl from the kitchen. (Serve)

offduty.speaker: Wilovan
offduty.text: None whatever, sir. My colleague is off attending an errand of the sort that keeps a man out past a decent hour, and I declined to attend it with him. A room where the fellow at the next table hasn't the first idea what I do, and no reason at all to ask, is a rare comfort. You'll note I've kept the hat on. That isn't a warning this evening. It's simply a good hat.

options.text: Bring him a bowl from the kitchen. (Serve)
"Then keep the chair as long as you like."

served.speaker: Wilovan
served.text: That's very kind, sir, and I shan't spoil it by haggling. A man in my line gets offered a great many things and pays for most of them one way or another. This is neither. Hat off for it, plain and slow, and then straight back on before the stew goes cold.
